Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 88404 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Here are my best bets for the Sunday and Monday slate in the NFL Week 9. Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings. Best of luck! Bengals (-3.5) vs Falcons: O/U 52.5 The Bengals and Falcons kick off in Madrid, Spain, at 9:30 AM Eastern Sunday morning, so set your alarm clocks, aka your phones! This should be a fantastic matchup, and I am looking at the Atlanta offense for a bounce-back spot. Last week against Tampa Bay, the Falcons lost in a monsoon as Michael Penix threw four interceptions, while the Atlanta defense was run. In sunny weather, we should expect the Falcons to look night and day. The Bengals are on a three-game winning streak over Miami, Baltimore, and Tennessee. Cam Ward threw for 304 yards and touchdowns, plus Tony Pollard ran for 117 yards and two scores on the Bengals. The Bengals’ four wins all come against teams with losing records so far, while the Falcons have shown their potential with wins over Green Bay and San Francisco. I still think the Falcons have the highest ceiling in the NFC South. I’ll take the +3.5 down to +3. Pick: Falcons +3.5 (1 unit) Giants (-3) at Eagles: O/U 38.5 For the first time since November 1, 2009, the New York Giants are favorites in Philadelphia, and that’s no mistake. Things are so bad during the Eagles’ six-game losing streak that they’ve benched Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton . Philadelphia has a bye week up next, so this is them 100-percent trying to see what they have before they decide on their intentions in the second half of the season. If the Eagles lose this game, they are borderline out of the postseason before Week 11 starts, but that desperation doesn’t interest me because they haven’t had any rhythm amid all the injuries. The Giants, on the other hand, are in first place in the division, coming out of a bye week after an impressive 27-21 OT win over Houston. New York has found something with J.J. McCarthy , and if Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers are bought in like they were against Houston (232 combined yards), then so am I. I like the Giants -3. Pick: Giants -3 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Packers at Patriots (-3): O/U 44.5 Green Bay has averaged a league-high 81.7% of their yards through the air, and 65.7% of their plays are passes. At some point, regression has to hit, and the backfield becomes more reliable. Josh Jacobs has started to turn the wheels of regression, but as we’ve seen through two games, it may take time. This matchup will be interesting since New England runs the third-most man coverage (29%). Love has completed 51% of his passes against man (25th) for 6.2 yards per attempt (6.2). Love’s faced a slew of bad defenses this season, and New England certainly isn’t bad. Christian Watson is a go, so I expect plenty of passes, but 37.5 is still steep despite Love throwing 41-plus times in three straight. I am going to sell high on Love and also go under Matthew Golden ‘s 68.5 receiving yards. Last week, Watson was very active before he suffered an injury that opened the door for Golden to sneak over his yards prop. Golden has gone over his yards prop in three of his last four games and saw 12-plus targets in three straight. However, Golden ranks 66th in target separation versus man coverage, and going up Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III won’t be easy. I’m going under on both Love and Golden. Picks: Jordan Love Under 37.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 69.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Cardinals at Seahawks (-8.5): O/U 39.5 Last week, I lost on Jaxon Smith-Njigba Under 101.5 receiving yards in garbage time, but you better believe I am running it back. JSN has been nothing short of spectacular. If the season ended today, he is the Offensive Player of the Year. JSN leads the league in receiving yards (985) and receiving touchdowns (9). He has four straight games with 100-plus receiving yards and seven out of eight on the season, but I am going Under. Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett away and will roll with Gardner Minshew for the meantime. Sam Darnold is out for Seattle, so Drew Lock will step up. Luckily for Lock, Seattle’s backfield is more crowded than ever and willing to assist. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet both returned in the last two weeks, plus George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson are capable backs. Arizona has lost 10 straight to Seattle, and after selling this past week, I could see the Seahawks rolling and working on their ground game. In Week 2 against Arizona with Lock at quarterback, Seattle ran the ball 40 times and threw it 26. JSN caught 155 of Lock’s 235 yards (11 targets). Ridiculous, but we could see a similar result here in play calling, capping JSN’s production. Pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Under 94.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Buccaneers at Bears (-6): O/U 47.5 Baker Mayfield has had the easiest job in the NFL over the last two weeks. Mayfield has thrown 14 passes in past two games. Against Atlanta, Mayfield and the Bucs became the first quarterback/team to not complete a pass since September 29, 1974! Mayfield went 0-for-3 and we might not see that feat happen for another 50 years. However, the good days are over. Welcome to the end times, Baker. You are in Chicago facing a white-hot Bears team with additions on the defense from trades and guys returning from injury. Mayfield won’t have the liberty of handing the ball to his talented backs like he has literally over 100 times in the last two games. I like all of Mayfield’s Overs this week, but my favorites are the attempts. Chicago leads the NFL in time of possession margin, so Mayfield will have to make his possessions count, and the Bears allow big plays through the air, so I’d expect Mayfield to take some shots downfield. Pick: Baker Mayfield Over 29.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Bills (-3) at Vikings: O/U 43.5 Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings as Kyler Murray deals with an injured hamstring. Minnesota is coming off their first loss of the season, 19-15 to the Lions. Buffalo was off a bye for a hyped up game against Baltimore, but due to two quarterback injuries, the Bills ended up routing the Ravens 36-10 in a game Buffalo never trailed. Buffalo gets two backup quarterbacks back-to-back weeks as they go for their fourth-straight win. I like the chances that happen. Buffalo leads the NFL in points per drive (3.07), and Minnesota is first in points allowed per drive (1.18). The Bills have been involved in the highest-scoring games and the Vikings the fewest. It’s a clash of offense versus defense, but I think offense will win. Minnesota has allowed two passing touchdowns since Week 2, but they’ve played Baker Mayfield , Malik Willis , Tyler Shough , Daniel Jones , and then Jared Goff last week. Josh Allen is on a different planet than those guys. I will gladly take Buffalo -3. I’d go out to -5.5. Contest --> Click to expand picks panel Click to open Sharp AI NFL Betting Primer, Picks & Predictions: Week 1 (2026) by Andrew Erickson | @AndrewErickson_ | Sep 11, 2026 by Andrew Erickson | @AndrewErickson_ | Sep 11, 2026 You smell that? That’s the smell of the first full Sunday slate of NFL action. For those who are just tuning into my featured weekly BettingPros piece for theted very first time, welcome! And for those coming back after last season…LFG. Glad to have you on board for another season of NFL betting action. This weekly piece has a simple goal. Help you identify the best bets and player props for the Sunday main slate (as I hit all the prime-time games in their own stand-alone betting primers). You can find all my 2026 betting articles here . What’s going to be different this year, beyond the intros (adding some personal touches), is the picks. I’m challenging myself to narrow down each main slate to five (ish) official picks: ATS/Total/ML. No more fluff. All gas. No brakes. Again, I’m bound to cover more than five actual bets in my analysis and breakdown of the marquee matchups. Five-six player props will also be included as the week progresses…even if they are added later in the week (injuries, man). But that will ensure all the games get covered in some capacity. Whether it’s an official play, a prop, or just a general lean. For Week 1, we’ve got six official plays from the rip (I’ve had a lot of time thinking about these Week 1 matchups). And when in doubt…take the under. The shift in 2026 is all about simplifying the process without sacrificing results. This will let me dive deeper into the games and trends I feel I have an advantage in… instead of forcing picks in matchups I don’t have a great read on. There are so many paths you can take to enrich your Sunday football experience, so let me be your guide. I’ve got my own fantasy football and betting knowledge, plus the tools on BettingPros to help push us over the top. Here’s to starting 2026 on a high note. I’m looking forward to an extremely fun Sunday. My niece is turning one. Happy Birthday, Claire! Excited to celebrate on Sunday, sweating out all my moneyline bets and unders. Uncle Erickson knows best. Because that’s the recipe for Week 1 (trends provided by BetMGM ). Fade Big Favorites Back Road Dogs (specifically divisional ones) Home underdogs (divisional) Teams that were good ATS in 2025 Since 2005, Week 1 unders have hit at a 55% rate. LFG. More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> For my thoughts on all the games on the Week 1 slate, be sure to check out the weekly lookahead lines show I do every week with Worm (Monday release following every Sunday slate) on the BettingPros YouTube Channel. Week 1 NFL Betting Primer Official Plays Houston Texans ML (+108) vs. Buffalo Bills Tennessee Titans ML (-108) vs. New York Jets Baltimore Ravens vs. Indianapolis Colts Under 48.5 (-113) Minnesota Vikings ML (-115) vs. Green Bay Packers Miami Dolphins ML (+115) vs. Las Vegas Raiders Jacksonville Jaguars -8.5 (-110) vs. Cleveland Browns Jonathan Taylor OVER 76.5 rushing yards vs. BAL (-115) Juwan Johnson OVER 42.5 receiving yards @ DET (-114) Greg Dulcich OVER 25.5 Receiving Yards @ LV (-120) Jalen Hurts UNDER 29.5 pass attempts VS WAS (-116) Quinshon Judkins UNDER 56.5 rushing yards Houston Texans vs. Buffalo Bills Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Texans to win, straight up (moneyline) Trends The home team has won each of the last 8 meetings in this series. Houston is the home team and is catching points. Texans finished 7-2 straight up at home in 2025. In 15 of 19 games last season, the Texans have covered +3.5 (79%). Houston has given Buffalo real trouble the last two seasons: road losses by 3 and 4 points (Oct. 2024: Texans 23, Bills 20; Nov. 2025: Texans 23, Bills 19). Josh Allen specifically has struggled against Houston across that stretch: 52.7% completion, 1 TD/2 INT, sacked 9 times combined in the losses. Each of the last five games between the Bills and Texans has gone UNDER the total points line. Since 2021, teams with an ATS percentage between 50 and 59% against prior playoff teams are 20-7 ATS, including 10-2 as a market favorite ( BetMGM ). Falcons, Texans, Vikings and Panthers qualify on the main Sunday slate Houston’s O/U record at home over 2024-2025 is 6-12 (6 overs, 12 unders) - a 66.7% Under rate at NRG Stadium across those two seasons. 2024 home games went 4-5 (Under-leaning, 55.6%), and 2025 home games went 2-7 - a much stronger 77.8% Early in the 2025 season, Houston opened 0-4 to the Under across their first four games league-wide (via SportsBettingDime). The Texans scored fewer than 40 combined points in 10 games in 2025. Overall The Houston Texans’ elite defense has given Josh Allen fits. The Bills QB has struggled in his last two matchups versus this defense, and I see no reason why 2026 will be much different. They added WR DJ Moore in the offseason, but it might not be enough to overcome the Texans’ suffocating defense. Houston was a Vegas home underdog (+6) and won outright last year versus Buffalo (Davis Mills started). Meanwhile, CJ Stroud – coming off reportedly his best training camp as a pro – has a much better matchup versus a softer Bills’ defense. Under a new defensive coordinator, Jim Leonhard, who is switching the scheme to a 3-4 defense, Buffalo will have some growing pains early on. Advantage Texans (who were the 5th-most injured offense last season). I also lean toward this game going under the total. These matchups have typically been more of a rock fight than an Old West shootout. I don’t need to sell anybody on Houston’s defense slowing down Buffalo, but keep in mind the Bills added to their defense this offseason. They added Bradley Chubb, CJ Gardner-Johnson, and Dee Alford at slot CB. They should have a healthy Ed Oliver. Drafted impact defensive players. They were the 4th-most injured defense last season. But without second-year WR Jayden Higgins (out for the season with a torn ACL) and OT Braden Smith on short-term IR…Houston’s offense still might stumble out of the gate. If David Montgomery is the engine of this Week 1 offense (especially given the Bills’ poor track record of stopping the run), this game could SLOG. Tennessee Titans vs. New York Jets Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Titans to win, straight up (moneyline) Trends Robert Saleh returns to face his old team in his Titans debut against the Jets, who fired him in Oct. 2024. Retread head coaches (previously an NFL HC elsewhere) have covered better at home than on the road since 2020: 48-43 ATS (52.7%) at home vs. 47-52 ATS (47.5%) on the road via VSIN. Saleh, as a retread HC, fits the favorable home bucket directly in this spot. Two defenses overhauled this offseason face off, supporting the lower-scoring game script. The Titans have scored first in eight of their last nine games. Injuries Titans Cedric Gray (LB - concussion) - Questionable Jets Breece Hall (RB - groin) - Questionable - trending toward playing per NFL.com Joseph Ossai (DE - foot) - Questionable - week-to-week per Rick Cimini Overall I’m taking the Titans to win at home in Week 1 versus the Jets. Robert Saleh is stepping in as the new HC, with a totally revamped defense (especially in the secondary). Just a few notable additions: John Franklin-Meyers, Jermaine Johnson, Anthony Hill, Alontae Taylor, Cor'Dale Flott, and Keldric Faulk. Saleh’s Jets defenses were borderline elite and helped him squeak out 7-win seasons with a carousel of QBs, including Zach Wilson, Mike White, Joe Flacco, and Trevor Siemian. And let’s not forget how he was able to make chicken salad out of chicken sh*t last year with the injury-plagued 49ers. Losing Gray (in concussion protocol after suffering a concussion in a UTV accident, according to Turron Davenport ) is a big deal given Gray's 164 tackles were the fourth most in the NFL this past season, per ESPN . But if anybody can combat defensive personnel injuries at linebacker…it’s Saleh. Expect the Titans’ second-round rookie LB, Anthony Hill Jr., to start. Tennessee also hired Brian Daboll as the new offensive coordinator, and he has a track record of success with developing young QBs (Josh Allen, Daniel Jones, Jaxson Dart, etc.). Cam Ward (despite his preseason woes) is slated to see a massive improvement in Year 2 with better coaching and actual weapons to throw to, between rookie Carnell Tate and free agent acquisition Wan'Dale Robinson. Saleh said after the second preseason game, the team ran its base vanilla offense. Regarding Tate: “When it's time to gameplan and get people the rock, we'll get him the rock.” He also praised the top-5 overall pick from this year’s draft for a strong training camp. Now back to Ward. The former first overall pick faced terrible circumstances as a rookie. Even so, during his last 7 games: 11 TDs (two rushing and 9 passing) and 1 pick. We see teams go from worst to first in the division every single year, and the Titans fit the bill to a tee as a major surprise team in 2026. Keep in mind that the Titans faced a BRUTAL schedule during Ward’s rookie year. Texans twice, Broncos, Rams, Chargers, Seattle, Jaguars twice, Browns, Chiefs. Per Sharp Football, Ward faced the most difficult schedule of pass defenses in 2025. They also played in 7 one-score games, going 2-5. The Jets secondary, featuring the likes of rookie D ‘ Angelo Ponds (out in Week 1), Nashon Wright, Azareye'h Thomas, and Brandon Stephens, will be a breath of fresh air for the Titans QB. Even if the second-year signal caller does throw an interception (regression for the Jets to get an interception will happen sooner rather than later), I expect the Titans to take care of business at home. Props Cam Ward OVER 0.5 interceptions Baltimore Ravens @ Indianapolis Colts Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Under 48.5 (total) Trends League-wide Week 1 Under bias: Unders have hit 55% of the time since 2005 per BetMGM, and 12 of last year’s Week 1 games went Under. NFL Week 1 Opener Unders – 54.6% since 2014. According to VSIN … Under total is on a historic 13-2 surge in the Ravens-Colts series. Daniel Jones is 34-15 under the total as an underdog since 2020 (VSIN). The Ravens have brand-new offensive/head-coaching setups calling plays for the first time together: Ravens HC Jesse Minter (hired after John Harbaugh was fired in Jan. 2026) and OC Declan Doyle are running Lamar Jackson’s offense for the first time in a live game - new-scheme Week 1s tend to play cautiously early. Daniel Jones (Colts) is making his first regular-season start since tearing his Achilles in Week 14 of 2025 - reportedly fully healthy, but first-game-back QBs are a real caution flag for offensive rhythm/scoring pace. Stud CB Sauce Gardner bolsters an Indianapolis secondary that should make Baltimore work for its yardage. The Colts’ defense overall is just underrated with Sauce, a healthy Charvarius Ward, and a dynamic defensive tackle duo of Grover Stewart/DeForest Buckner plugging up the interior. Injuries Colts Daniel Jones (QB - Achilles (2025 tear)) - Off report - fully cleared, first action back Alec Pierce (WR - recovering from offseason ankle/heel surgery) - Expected to play Ravens Zay Flowers (WR - lower body) - Questionable, expected to play per beat reporter Nnamdi Madubuike (DT - neck) - Out Teddye Buchanan (LB - knee) - Out Overall Taking the under in any dome game featuring Lamar Jackson is terrifying (especially in Week 1 with a new offensive play caller). Fast track in Indy has been as advertised. Seventeen of the Colts’ last 26 games at Lucas Oil Stadium have gone OVER the total points line. And unfortunately, the line movement is not working in our favor – given the total has dropped from 49.5 points to 48.5 points (47.5 on some other sportsbooks). And the 2025 Colts beat down on Jesse Minter's strong Chargers defense last season - 38 to 24 (most points LAC allowed all season). I think all the question marks regarding the Colts’ offense between their QB and WRs are very real. So to me, I think this just might be a monster 30-touch Jonathan Taylor game to keep pressure off Jones in his first action back. JT was very productive versus Minter’s defense last season, and this team tends to ride or die on their workhorse RB. 16 carries, 94 yards, and 3 TDs last year versus the Bolts. Usually a run-heavy game script backs the under…but not when it’s a guy like Taylor. Especially against a defensive front like Baltimore…where DT Nnamdi Madubuike is still not a lock to play in Week 1 (coming off a season-ending neck injury). Calais Campbell can only do so much as a 40-year-old defensive tackle. Worm mentioned this in the Week 1 early lookahead show that this was his favorite UNDER on the slate. He also mentioned this Mike Madonald/Minter-style defense allows some rushing production, which I think the Colts will gladly jump at with a healthy Taylor. A strong run game also alleviates the potential pass rush of the Ravens’ newcomer off the edge, Trey Hendrickson. He will have his fair share of opportunities against new Colts RT, Jalen Travis, in Week 1. Conversely, I don’t think the Ravens’ run game will be as productive. I highlighted the Stewart/Buckner dynamic in the trends section as major upgrades to the Colts’ run defense. Pair that with the Ravens starting Jovaughn Gwyn at center (major downgrade from Tyler Linderbaum), and that’s a cause for concern. Baltimore is set to have three new starters on the offensive line, all in the interior. And Derrick Henry did show some signs of slowing down last season. Career-low elusive rating in 2025- middle of the pack last season. 14th-lowest missed tackles forced per attempt YPC falls from 5.6 YPC to 4.7 without tight end Charlie Kolar (Chargers TE1). From Weeks 1-10, Henry’s missed tackle-forced rate of 12.8% was the lowest among running backs (min. 60 carries). But I’d be lying if I wasn’t afraid of what Henry could do if he gets to the second level against a lighter LB core featuring Akeem Davis-Gathers and rookie CJ Allen. Process still says we want to lean UNDERs in Week 1, and as one of the highest totals on the slate, that is still my preferred way to attack this matchup (along with JT props). Speaking of which. Take the OVER on Taylor’s 76.5 rushing yards prop. He cleared this number in 54% of his games last season with Daniel Jones, including 5/7 at home. He has averaged over 100 rushing yards per game at home during his NFL career. Props Jonathan Taylor OVER 76.5 rushing yards Jacksonville Jaguars vs. Cleveland Browns Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Jaguars -8.5 Trends The Browns are 2-11 ATS in their last 13 road games Cleveland traded All-Pro EDGE Myles Garrett to the Rams this offseason - a major downgrade to the Browns’ pass rush and overall defense. Browns QB Deshaun Watson is making his first regular-season start since October 2024, coming off a torn Achilles that required two surgeries - first-start rust is a genuine risk factor working in Jacksonville’s favor. Jaguars went 7-2 ATS at home last season (first) and finished first in average scoring margin at home (+13.7). The Browns ranked fourth-worst last season (-11.6) in average scoring margin on the road last season. Injuries Jaguars LeQuint Allen Jr. (RB - soft-tissue) - GTD Cole Van Lanen (RT – knee) – GTD Browns Maliek Collins (DT – Quad) – Limited Teven Jenkins (OG – Back) – Limited – Confirmed out. Overall You will only get so many opportunities to fade Deshaun Watson. And against the Jaguars, a team that definitely hasn’t gotten enough publicity after how strong they finished the 2025 season? This one is an absolute layup for me. Last season, the Jaguars ran up the score on bad teams like the Titans and Jets. Jacksonville went 7-2 ATS at home last season and finished first in average scoring margin at home (+13.7). The Browns are a completely different defense on the road. The Browns ranked fourth-worst last season (-11.6) in average scoring margin on the road last season. No Myles Garrett, and no defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger only recently returned to practice after missing nearly four weeks with an undisclosed injury. DT Maliek Collins is coming off a torn quad injury (still listed on the injury report). The Jaguars finished 2025 with the third-toughest matchup against RBs. Fourth-lowest YPC. Fewest rushing yards allowed. They have a very similar starting defense, sans linebacker Devin Lloyd, CB Greg Newsome, and S Andrew Wingard from last season. They also traded for DL Ruke Orhorhoro to further bolster their front-7. Quinshon Judkins surpassed 56.5 rushing yards once in his last five road games during his rookie season. The Brownies, as touchdown underdogs behind a brand-new starting O-line with Watson under center, are a recipe for an offensive disaster. Bad OLs don't travel. And OG Teven Jenkins is already banged up . Lay the points with DUVAL. Wouldn’t surprise me if they win by at least two touchdowns. Props Quinshon Judkins UNDER 56.5 rushing yards Minnesota Vikings vs. Green Bay Packers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Vikings to win, straight up (moneyline) Trends When the 2026 schedule was released in May, Green Bay opened as 1.5-point favorites (Vikings +1.5) - Minnesota WAS the “divisional home underdog”. The number has since moved a full 3 points to Vikings -1.5. Micah Parsons (Packers) is confirmed OUT for Week 1 - on PUP with a knee/ACL issue, targeting a return around Week 5. Green Bay went 0-4 (0-5-1 ATS, one push in their last six games) the rest of the way after his Week 15 injury last season. Vikings are 4-2 ATS within the division and have won 9 of their last 13 home games. GB is just 3-7 ATS on the road in their last 10 appearances (third-worst). Eight of the Vikings’ last nine games have gone UNDER the total points line. Since 2021, teams with an ATS percentage between 50 and 59% against prior playoff teams are 20-7 ATS, including 10-2 as a market favorite (BetMGM). The Vikings are the lone “favored” qualifier on the main Sunday slate Kyler Murray – Per StatMuse – is 3-2-1 SU in six career Week 1 appearances (5-1 ATS). Overall I was all over the Vikings ML play when these Week 1 lines first dropped back in May. Divisional home underdog? Easy money. The lines have since moved dramatically in favor of the Vikings, after it was announced that Kyler Murray would be the team’s starting QB. Murray has always started seasons hot, just to fizzle out in the second half (right around late October/early November when a certain video game FPS has its annual release). The new Vikings QB is 9-11-1 in September and 15-9 in October for a 24-20-1 combined record through the first two months of the year (53%). The remaining months? 14-28 (33%). Woof. But backing the Vikings is more about fading the Packers. They couldn’t be trusted to win any games last year without star edge rusher Micah Parsons. They were also bad on the road (4-6 SU). The Packers also lost their DC, Jeff Hafley, replacing him with former Cardinals HC Jonathan Gannon. I think the Gannon matchup against Kyler Murray is fascinating. We discussed it more in-depth on the Tailgate Show, where both Alfredo Brown and Derek Brown cited it as a reason to be in on GB in this spot. But if Gannon is familiar with Murray’s strengths and weaknesses, Murray knows this defense as well (which also wasn’t particularly great in Arizona). The argument works both ways, in my opinion. I think the Minnesota run game is being undersold here. RB Jordan Mason got a lot of hype this offseason, and I like his odds to be even more productive behind a healthy Vikings offensive line. This Packers’ DL is being front-lined by a lot of players coming off season-ending injuries (Devonte Wyatt). FA acquisition and former Vikings player Javon Hargrave is 33 years old and missed a lot of training camp with a knee injury (listed on the Week 1 injury report). And defensively, Minnesota is never an easy out with defensive coordinator Brian Flores dialing up his unique pressures. This Packers OL (bottom-5 by consensus rankings) will have its work cut out for them. Jordan Morgan is not only making the switch from guard to tackle, but he is also dealing with a lingering knee issue. One of just three Packers’ offensive linemen who are battling injuries. Minnesota ranked first in pressure rate in 2025 (44.5%). Jordan Morgan was a limited participant in practice today with a knee injury. On the first injury report of the season for the Packers, three of their preferred starting offensive linemen-Aaron Banks, Zach Bako-Bewele, and Morgan-are hindered by knee issues. — Zach Jacobson (@zachjacobson) September 9, 2026 Miami Dolphins vs. Las Vegas Raiders Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick : Dolphins to win, straight up (moneyline) - “Upset of the Week” Trends Kirk Cousins was named the Raiders’ new starting QB for 2026, over rookie Fernando Mendoza. The Dolphins beat a Cousins-led Falcons team 34-10 last season. Las Vegas’s new HC is Klint Kubiak and Miami’s new HC is Jeff Hafley, and both are making their first NFL head-coaching debuts this week. Per VegasInsider: Rookie HCs are 42-39-2 ATS in home openers since 2002, but just 8-14-1 ATS in home openers since 2016 - and rookie HCs favored -3.5 or more at home specifically are only 10-11 ATS (despite going 15-6 SU). The Raiders are only 3-point favorites. Injuries Raiders Ashton Jeanty (RB - ankle) - Questionable - Expected to play Brock Bowers (TE - out) Overall I’ve been on the Miami Dolphins’ upset train at Las Vegas since the schedule release in May. And that was with full acknowledgment of the roster discrepancies between these two franchises. The Raiders have a better team on paper, and they were projected to have the best offensive player in the game (Brock Bowers). But with Bowers out due to his meniscus, I feel even more strongly about Miami coming away with the upset. Last year without their star TE, the Raiders looked lost offensively. They went 2-3 SU/ATS, but their point differential was insane. They were outscored by 77 points (15.4 PPG). Losing him matters a lot, given the Dolphins’ glaring weakness is their secondary. Do the Raiders have the pass-catchers between Michael Mayer, Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, and Jack Bech to take advantage of the league’s worst secondary? With Kirk Cousins under center? I remain skeptical given what we saw from Cousins last season. His 6.4 YPA and 84.8 passer rating were the second-lowest of his career last season (same with aDOT). He doesn't have the same power in his throws since his Achilles injury: 34th in EPA/play, 26th in success rate, 28th in completion rate, 32nd in YPA. Miami does have some talent at LB and on their DL (Chop Robinson, Jordyn Brooks, Jacob Rodriguez), so I think they can at least do something against Cousins, given his subpar weaponry. Although they will not have last year’s first-rounder, Kenneth Grant. I also do not fear the Raiders’ defense in any capacity under their new DC, Rob Leonard. He’s been the DL coach since 2023. Leonard is an unproven commodity who will face a new-look Malik Willis Miami offense sure to feature plenty of new wrinkles Las Vegas can’t fully prepare for. Leonard’s scheme is similar to Seattle’s Mike Macdonald, which suggests plenty of QB rushes and RB/TE targets. Exactly what you want to hear if you are the Dolphins’ OC, Bobby Slowik. Expect plenty of Willis rushing attempts and De’Von Achane targets out of the backfield. Hafley also coached the opposing Raiders’ new starting LB, Quay Walker, in Green Bay. Overall, the Raiders’ interior defensive line projects as a weakness Miami can exploit. Because I also think the Dolphins’ OL is underrated. The projected starting 5 is one of the league’s youngest units, which underscores their upside. All in all, the 3-point line just suggests to me the Raiders are the home team. Neither roster is good, and it’s two rookie head coaches going H2H (where the home coach has struggled to cover the number). When I don’t see a clear advantage with the favored team (especially in Week 1), I love the underdog here. Give me the unknown upside of Willis with Achane, Greg Dulcich, and some plucky rookie WRs against a 38-year-old immobile QB without his best receiver. Willis ranked first in EPA/play last season. Cousins ranked 34th. Fins. Up. No. 2 moneyline bet in the Smart Money Tool on BettingPros? The Dolphins. Sharps are backing the Dolphins moneyline at + 150 (based on $32K in prediction market liquidity). And speaking of Dulcich…let’s talk props. Dulcich OVER 25.5 yards. He hit the over in his last 5 games played with the Miami Dolphins last season. Over 21.5 receiving yards in all but one of his last nine games played. The line has moved since it opened at 16.5 yards, but I still like the over play here against the Raiders LB/S room. Isaiah Pola-Mao was PFF’s 4th-worst graded coverage safety last season. Jeremy Chinn allowed the 8th-highest passer rating when targeted. Walker allowed the 5th-most yards as a coverage linebacker last season in Green Bay. Props Greg Dulcich Over 25.5 Receiving Yards Remaining Matchups Pittsburgh Steelers vs. Atlanta Falcons Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Steelers -6, Under 40.5 Trends The Falcons have failed to cover the spread in each of their last four Week 1 road games. Falcons starting QB Michael Penix Jr. is OUT for Week 1 with a third ACL tear - newly signed Tua Tagovailoa is expected to be the Week 1 starter, a significant continuity downgrade with this specific roster. Atlanta is also down two starting edge rushers: Jalon Walker (torn ACL in camp, season-ending IR) and James Pearce Jr. (suspended through Week 9) - a thin pass rush heading into Acrisure Stadium. Since 2024, the Steelers are 6-2 ATS at home as a favorite. Since 2024, the Steelers are 11-6 ATS overall at home. The Steelers have won the first half in each of their last seven of their last 8 games at Acrisure Stadium Injuries Steelers Joey Porter Jr. (CB – Back) - Wants a new contract and might not play, according to Andrew Fillipponi . Falcons Tua Tagovailoa (QB – Oblique) appeared to suffer an oblique injury during practice on Thursday. Confirmed out. Cooper Rush will start. Jawaan Taylor (RT – Knee) Overall This is such a tough spot for Atlanta. On the road outdoors without Tua Tagovailoa. Steelers play better at home, and I think this one is a layup. This was one of Seth’s best bets on our Week 1 BettingPros betting show, and I see no reason to go in the opposite direction. Screams like a positive Rico Dowdle game script where he can feast as a rusher and find the end zone against a lackluster Falcons’ defensive line. Props Rico Dowdle anytime TD (+125) Tampa Bay Buccaneers vs. Cincinnati Bengals Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Tampa Bay +3.5 Injuries Buccaneers Sean Tucker (RB – Hamstring) Bengals Shermar Stewart (DE – Knee) – Doubtful DJ Turner (CB – Hamstring) Trends: This unusually high 50.5+ total lines up with Cincinnati’s 2025 defense: 30th in points allowed and 31st in yards allowed. Tampa Bay was one of the league’s worst ATS teams in 2025 - 5-12 ATS, tied for the league’s worst mark. The Buccaneers failed to cover the spread in each of their last nine games. Each of the Bengals’ last four season openers have gone UNDER the total points line. Week 1 carries a mild historical Under lean overall (~55% since 2005) - a modest counterweight to how this total is being priced. Twelve of the Bengals’ last 16 home games have gone OVER the total points line (6-3 in 2025 toward the Over; 12-5 since 2024; 8-3 as home favorite toward Over) Since 2023, the Buccaneers are 61% ATS as an underdog 63% ATS on the road 68% as a road underdog Overall When do we bet on the Buccaneers and Baker Mayfield? When they are underdogs on the road. When do we fade the Bengals? Week 1. Take the Bucs with the points. New Orleans Saints vs. Detroit Lions Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Over 49.5 Injuries Saints Cameron Jordan (EDGE – Hamstring) – Ruled out. Lions Brian Branch (S -PUP) Kerby Joseph (S -PUP) Trends 16 of the Lions’ last 23 home games have gone over the total - and Detroit’s covered that Over as a favorite in 12 of its last 15 home games as the chalk. The Lions’ last 34 home games have averaged 55.1 points, with 71% of those games (25-of-35) hitting at least 51 points. Ford Field is still the Coors Field of the NFL. Detroit has hit the Over in 12 of its last 13 Week 1 games and gone 7-1 ATS in its last 8 September games. New Orleans is 2-8 ATS in its last 10 Week 1 games. New Orleans is committed to 2025 2nd-round pick Tyler Shough at QB - won 4 of his final 5 rookie starts, but the offense averaged under 20 points/game across those 9 starts. Very easy schedule against bottom-ranked teams/defenses. Eight of the Saints’ last nine games as underdogs have gone UNDER the total points line. Overall: Never saw a game total in Detroit that I didn’t like the over in. Two dome teams going head-to-head…points are coming. Shootout game environment. All the overs. The Lions’ secondary is still a total mess. Starting safety duo of Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph are still hurt. And this Saints’ pass rush outside of Chase Young is non-existent. Veteran edge rusher Cameron Jordan has already been ruled out with a hamstring injury. And that brings me to my favorite player prop: Saints tight end Juwan Johnson over 42.5 receiving yards. After the team moved on from Rashid Shaheed last season, Johnson cleared this mark in 5 of his last 8 games. As the clear-cut No. 2 receiver on the Saints offense behind Chris Olave, Johnson should FEAST in a high-scoring matchup. Johnson finished 5th in catches (77) and third in yards (889) among TEs in 2025. But he only scored three TDs. TD regression hitting in Week 1? You bet. Props: Juwan Johnson OVER 42.5 receiving yards Juwan Johnson anytime TD (+240) Chicago Bears versus Carolina Panthers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Over 47.5, Panthers +3 Trends Carolina was excellent as a home underdog in 2025 - 8 times in that spot, covering 6 and winning 5 outright - and they’re a home dog again here (+3.5). Panthers’ O-line is thin: LT Ikem Ekwonu (torn knee ligament, opens on PUP) and RT Taylor Moton (blood clots, Reserve/NFI) are both out, forcing two new starters in - real risk to Bryce Young’s protection. 2025 ATS form was strong for both sides: Bears went 12-7 ATS, Panthers went 11-7 ATS. Bears went 6-2-1 to the Over on the road in 2025; Panthers went 5-4 Over at home but 10-8 Under overall for the season. Twelve of the Panthers’ last 16 games at Bank of America Stadium have gone OVER the total points line. The Panthers have covered the spread in each of their last 11 games following a loss (covered 14 straight as underdogs following a loss). The Panthers are 14-7 over/under after a loss since 2024. Eight of the Panthers’ last 12 games at home as underdogs have gone over the total points line Injuries Bears Rome Odunze (WR – Calf) – Says will play. Ozzy Trapilo (OT – Knee) – Questionable Overall: The Panthers are coming off a playoff loss and catching points at home against the most hyped team during the preseason. Take the underdog, and bet the over. Bank of America Stadium isn’t the Coors Field of the NFL, but it’s the Coors Lite version. Chicago might have the worst defense in the NFL that even Bryce Young and company can put points on. No. 1 moneyline bet in the Smart Money Tool on BettingPros? The Cardiac Cats. Sharps are backing the Panthers moneyline at +150 (based on $363K in prediction market liquidity). Arizona Cardinals vs. Los Angeles Chargers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Cardinals +9.5 Trends Arizona’s 2025 season completely collapsed - finished 3-14 with a franchise-record 9-game losing streak to close the year, got HC Jonathan Gannon fired, and released Kyler Murray (now Minnesota’s starter). By contrast, the Chargers return everything intact: HC Jim Harbaugh and QB Justin Herbert, coming off a second straight playoff berth under Harbaugh. But they also added OC Mike McDaniel as an upgrade from Greg Roman. NFL underdogs have covered 56.8% of Week 1 games since 2019 (road dogs 59.0%, underdogs of 6+ points 60.7%) - a legitimate situational trend working against laying double digits here, regardless of how bad Arizona looked closing out 2025. Rookie head coaches have struggled in the large underdog role, going 27-114 SU (19%) and 67-74 ATS (47%) when catching 7 points or more since 2017 (VSIN). Five of the Chargers’ last six games have gone UNDER the total points line. The Cardinals are 4-8 against the spread (ATS) with Jacoby Brissett as the starting quarterback (1-8 in the last nine starts). They are 9-4 toward the OVER. The Cardinals have covered the spread in seven of their last 11 games as road underdogs. In 2025, Arizona was within one score in all but seven games (2-8 record in close games). Trey McBride has scored at least one touchdown in 8 of the Cardinals’ last 9 games as road underdogs. According to VSIN , underdogs of 6.5 points or more might be just 11-34-1 SU, but they are 32-13-1 ATS (71.1%) in Week 1 since 2013. Injuries Cardinals Jeremiyah Love (RB – Ankle) – In Garrett Williams (CB – Achilles) – Out Chargers Keaton Mitchell (RB – Hamstring) Overall I love the Chargers in 2026, but laying this many points for no home-field advantage feels like a trap. The Arizona Cardinals defense is much healthier than it was last season, and they have enough offensive weapons for a backdoor cover. They added a lot of defensive depth upfront this offseason, and the Bolts will be starting a rookie center in Week 1. I won’t go as far as Arizona winning outright, but I think they might give those Chargers’ Survivor picks quite the scare. These late-afternoon window games can get weird, and it would be so on brand for the Chargers to come out flat as 9.5-point favorites. Washington Commanders vs. Philadelphia Eagles Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: Eagles -5.5, Under 44.5 Trends According to VSIN , Nick Sirianni boasts a 26-6 SU and 20-11 ATS record as a single-digit home favorite since 2021 Eight of the Eagles’ last 10 games have gone under the total points line (the two overs coming versus the Washington Commanders) The Eagles are 11-22-2 ATS when their defense has allowed 20+ points since the start of last season. The Eagles are 6-14 over/under at home since the start of 2024 (fewer than 44 points per game). Thirteen of the Eagles’ last 17 home games have gone under the total points line. Philly has scored 26-plus points in four of the last five games versus the Commanders, coached by Dan Quinn. Over the total is 7-1 in the last eight of the Commanders-Eagles divisional series The Eagles have won 11 of their last 12 home games against NFC East opponents. The Eagles are 22-5-2 ATS when their defense has allowed fewer than 20 points since the start of 2024 (75%). The Eagles are 6-13 O/U at home since the start of 2024 (<44 PPG). 12 of the Eagles’ last 16 home games have gone UNDER the total points line. When Washington allows 20 points or fewer on defense, they are 12-4 toward the Under; when they allow at least 20 points on defense, they are 30-8 toward the OVER (79%). The Commanders have lost 10 of their last 12 games. Injuries Eagles Jonathan Greenard (EDGE – Pectoral) Commanders K’Lavon Chaisson (EDGE – Knee) Jacory Croskey-Merritt (RB – Groin) Odafe Oweh (EDGE – Calf) Overall Philadelphia Eagles’ home games lean toward the under. Philly is unveiling a brand-new offense under Sean Mannion, so there’s bound to be some growing pains. It’s still a new install of an offense, so I’d expect them to dial up a fast pace of play. Take the under at the Linc, and lay the points with the home team. Given that, I love the under on the Eagles’ QB pass attempts. Mannion comes from the Green Bay Packers coaching tree – notorious for never letting Jordan Love cook. We should see something similar with Jalen Hurts in Week 1. Packers +2.5 vs. Bears: Chicago has been the better team through four weeks, but I think this number is giving the Bears a little too much credit on the road. The Bears rank ninth in offensive EPA per play and fifth in defensive EPA per play, while Green Bay has struggled badly on offense, ranking 26th in EPA per play. The concern is obvious, but there were legitimate signs of improvement last week. Jordan Love produced +0.14 EPA per play against Tampa Bay and earned a 77.9 PFF offensive grade, his best performance of the season. Love’s season-long PFF grade is still just 55.1, but this is also a stylistic matchup that gives him a chance to improve. PFF notes Love has been efficient against man coverage, and Chicago ranks second in man-coverage rate. Green Bay is also at home in a divisional game where getting +2.5 provides some protection in what I expect to be a one-score game. Jaguars -7 vs. Eagles: This is one of the biggest EPA mismatches on the board. Jacksonville ranks fourth in offensive EPA per play, while Philadelphia ranks 27th defensively. The gap widens on the ground, where the Jaguars rank fourth in rushing EPA per carry, and the Eagles rank 29th against the run. Jacksonville also owns a major passing edge, ranking fourth in EPA per dropback against a Philadelphia defense ranked 22nd. The other side is just as concerning for Philadelphia. The Eagles rank 29th in offensive EPA per play and 25th in passing EPA per dropback. Jalen Hurts owns only a 62.8 overall PFF grade and a 58.6 passing grade, ranking 25th among qualified quarterbacks. Jacksonville also enters with a league-best +6 turnover differential and six interceptions through four games. If the Jaguars get ahead early, they have the rushing efficiency and defensive advantage to turn this into a comfortable win. Bhayshul Tuten over 14.5 carries: This is probably my favorite matchup-specific angle of the group. Jacksonville ranks fourth in rushing EPA per carry, while Philadelphia ranks 29th in defensive rushing EPA. That is a massive 25-place gap, and it lines up perfectly with Tuten’s growing role in the offense. Tuten has 60 carries for 277 yards through four games and has been even better than the raw numbers suggest. His 90.3 overall PFF grade ranks second among qualified running backs, while his 89.1 rushing grade ranks first. He has forced 19 missed tackles and is averaging 4.02 yards after contact per attempt. Last week, he handled 17 carries compared with just six for Chris Rodriguez, making it clear Jacksonville is leaning toward Tuten as its primary runner. New England ranks only 23rd in offensive EPA per play, 21st in passing EPA and 23rd in rushing EPA. That becomes especially important against a Raiders defense that ranks fourth in overall defensive EPA, fifth against the pass and seventh against the run. Las Vegas has quietly been one of the more efficient defenses in football through four weeks. The Patriots defense can also create problems for Las Vegas. New England ranks sixth in defensive passing EPA, while the Raiders are only 14th overall offensively and 29th in rushing EPA. That should force Las Vegas to rely heavily on its passing game rather than control the matchup on the ground—Fourth and Data projects only 44 combined points, below the market total of 45.5. 49ers vs. Seahawks under 47.5: This is a strength-on-strength matchup that should be more defensive than the names on offense suggest. San Francisco ranks first in offensive EPA per play, but Seattle ranks second defensively. The Seahawks are especially strong against the pass, ranking fourth in defensive passing EPA and second against the run. San Francisco will have to earn almost everything underneath rather than relying on explosives. Seattle’s offense has more concerns. The Seahawks rank only 13th in offensive EPA per play, 28th in rushing EPA and 31st on third down. San Francisco has also been excellent at preventing explosive plays, allowing them on just 2.7% of snaps, the best in the NFL. Seattle is third at 4.9%. That combination points toward longer drives, fewer chunk plays, and fewer easy touchdowns. At 47.5, I’m comfortable betting this game stays in the low-to-mid 40s. NFL Week 5 expert picks The slate has multiple openings that are solid-looking plays for Week 5. Here is a roundup of the most attractive spreads, moneyline, and total bets. Best NFL Week 5 spread bets Jaguars -7 vs. Eagles ( -115 at DraftKings ) The Eagles are a mess right now, and I don’t think a trip to London fixes it. Philadelphia has dropped two straight, including blowing a 10-point lead late in a 24-20 loss to the Rams, and they’re the only team in the NFL that hasn’t covered a spread yet this season. The offense is the biggest problem. Jalen Hurts is averaging just 6.3 yards per attempt, his lowest mark since he took over as the starter, and the offensive line is getting beat up so badly that he barely has time to read the field. On top of that, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, and Dallas Goedert are all questionable, and Lane Johnson is on the injury report too. That’s a rough setup against this Jacksonville defense. The Jaguars have been one of the league's best teams at stopping the run, which means Philadelphia will likely have to put this game on Hurts’ arm. Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence has the Jags at 3-1 with wins over the Browns, Patriots, and Bengals. Seven points is a big number to lay, but Jacksonville has been dominant as a favorite under Liam Coen, and I trust them to pull away late. Raiders +3.5 vs. Patriots ( -110 at FanDuel ) The Raiders are the only team in the league that’s 4-0 against the spread, and I’m not ready to fade them yet. They fell to the Chiefs last week, but they hung right there with one of the best teams in the AFC, and that told me this start is legit. Kirk Cousins has been a big part of it. He’s tied for the league lead with 11 touchdown passes and has been excellent over his last eight starts. The Las Vegas defense also deserves credit, as they’ve held opponents under 60% passing in three of their four games. That said, Drake Maye is coming off his best game of the season. He threw three touchdowns and ran for 54 yards in the comeback win over Buffalo and took home AFC Offensive Player of the Week. Before that, though, he really struggled through the first three weeks, and he’s still getting pressured at a high rate. One big game doesn’t erase that for me. This line was 8.5 before the season, and I think the hook on 3.5 is valuable in what should be a close, lower-scoring game. Falcons -3.5 vs. Ravens ( -115 at DraftKings ) This line has swung nine points since the lookahead, and it’s all about Lamar Jackson. He sprained his ankle against the Titans and reportedly has only an outside chance to play Sunday night, which would put Tyler Huntley under center. The drop-off without Jackson is real. The Ravens are 6-11 without him since 2019, and they were shut out in the second half against Tennessee after he left the game. Baltimore’s offensive line has also been a problem, and Derrick Henry hasn’t been as productive this season. Without Jackson’s legs as a threat, it gets even tougher for Henry to find room. Atlanta, meanwhile, is rolling. The Falcons have outscored their last two opponents 80-38, including a blowout of the Saints on Monday night. They’re on a short week, which is worth noting, but I like them at home in prime time against a Baltimore team that likely won’t have their best player. MORE: Benefits of line shopping in betting Best NFL Week 5 moneyline bets Vikings to win ML vs. Saints ( -110 at DraftKings ) The Vikings haven’t been pretty, but they’re 4-0 and one of just three unbeaten teams left in the league. The offense has been a grind, and they failed to find the end zone in two of those wins. That said, the defense has carried them every single week, and I don’t see that changing against a struggling Saints team. New Orleans is 1-3 and coming off a 45-24 beatdown by the Falcons on Monday night. That means a short week of prep, and the Saints have already dropped two straight at the Superdome, including a 35-27 loss to the Raiders. Minnesota should also get a big offensive boost. Justin Jefferson sat out last week with an ankle injury but is expected back, and he gets a Saints secondary that’s been one of the worst in the league. Kyler Murray hasn’t had much working through the air yet, but having Jefferson back against this defense is exactly what he needs. I’d rather take the Vikings to win than lay the points with an offense that’s been this inconsistent. Jets to win ML vs. Browns ( -135 at FanDuel ) I know this one looks a little ugly on paper. The Jets are 1-3 and coming off a sloppy 23-12 loss in Chicago where they committed 12 penalties, and Geno Smith had his worst game of the season. But I think the market is overreacting a bit to one bad afternoon. Before that game, the Jets defense was one of the stingiest in the league, giving up the second-fewest yards per game through three weeks. Smith had also played well in his return to New York, and the Jets were right there in a 31-24 loss to the Lions the week before. This team has been more competitive than their record says. Meanwhile, the Browns are 3-1, but they’ve been living on the edge. Deshaun Watson has needed a fourth-quarter comeback in all three wins, and the last one took a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left to beat the Steelers. Cleveland was also flagged 14 times in that game and lost Mason Graham to a knee injury early. I’ll back the Jets at home to get back on track in a low-scoring game. MORE: Everything to know about moneyline betting Best NFL Week 5 over/under bets 49ers vs. Seahawks under 47.5 ( -115 at FanDuel ) This one sets up as a slugfest between two of the best defenses in the league. The Seahawks and 49ers rank first and second in defensive explosive-play rate, so neither team is giving up many chunk plays, and that makes it tough for a game to get out of hand on the scoreboard. Seattle’s defense has been especially nasty. Through three weeks, the Seahawks led the NFL in total defense, allowing just 3.8 yards per play. The offense hasn’t been nearly as reliable, though. Seattle is without Jadarian Price and has really struggled to run the ball, which could leave them leaning on Sam Darnold more than they’d like against a tough 49ers front. To be fair, the 49ers offense has been rolling and is a big reason they’re 4-0. That said, these two teams know each other well, and their two regular-season meetings last year both went way under the total. I expect another physical, grind-it-out divisional game in Seattle. Raiders vs. Patriots under 45.5 ( -115 at DraftKings ) The under has hit in three of the Patriots’ four games this season, and I think this matchup points the same way. New England’s offense has had its ups and downs, and a lot of that comes down to protection. Drake Maye was pressured on nearly half of his dropbacks against Buffalo, and he’s been far less effective when he doesn’t have a clean pocket. That plays right into what the Raiders do well. When Las Vegas gets home, opposing quarterbacks have averaged under 5 yards per attempt, which is among the best marks in the league. If they can keep collapsing the pocket, New England will have a hard time stringing together long drives. The Raiders offense could also be a little short-handed. Ashton Jeanty is questionable with a sprain, and losing him would take away a big piece of their ground game. Add in a long cross-country trip for Las Vegas, and I like this game to stay on the lower side of the number. In Weeks 1-6, Green Bay had a 65.9% pass rate, and last week they actually bumped it a tad higher to 70.8%. Overall, they have the second-best passing rate in the NFL. Among 34 qualifying passers, Love has still struggled with accuracy, ranking 22nd in passing success rate and 28th in catchable target rate, but he is also tenth in hero throw rate and 14th in passing touchdown rate. This week, Love will have a tougher matchup. Since Week 4, Carolina has continued to field a strong pass defense, allowing the 11th-fewest yards per attempt, the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the 13th-lowest passing success rate. Love has the volume, the talent, and the skilled receivers to overcome a strong pass defense. Josh Jacobs (RB) Last week, in his first game back, Josh Jacobs was the RB7 in fantasy scoring. He played 53.8% of the snaps with 57.9% of the rushing workload, a 43.5% route share, and a 15.6% target share. Jacobs had an 11.1% explosive run rate, 1.45 yards after contact per attempt, and a 9% missed tackle rate. Those aren’t amazing numbers (outside of the explosive run rate), but it’s a one-game sample, so I’m not freaking out. Jacobs finished with 16 touches and 91 total yards. It was a more substantial workload than I thought he’d get in his first game back, but five of those touches were receptions. His 11 carries were about what I thought he would see. Jacobs should have another strong game this week. Since Week 3, Carolina has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the eighth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-most yards after contact per attempt. Tetairoa McMillan (WR) Tetairoa McMillan is the WR13 in fantasy points per game. This week McMillan faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four games with Coker as a full-go, McMillan has had a 21% TPRR and 2.67 YPRR against two high. McMillan has a nice shot at a bounce-back game this week against a Green Bay secondary that (since Week 3) has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers. Jalen Coker (WR) Jalen Coker didn’t have the massive game last week that I was projecting, as Carolina’s passing offense cratered as Bryce Young fell back to Earth. Coker could have a bounce-back outing this week. In his four full games this season, Coker has had a 22.2% target share with 2.40 YPRR, five red zone targets, eight deep targets, and a 30.2% first-read share. Overall, he is the WR22 in fantasy points per game. This week, Coker faces a Green Bay defense that has the third-highest two-high rate in the NFL (66.3%). In those four full games, against two-high, Coker has had a 23% TPRR with 1.85 YPRR. Bryce Young will have to look like his early-season form for this passing attack to have bite again, but it’s possible. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game while ranking 15th in yards per target allowed to perimeter wide receivers. Last week, Young completed only 51.8% of his passes with 163 passing yards (6.4 yards per attempt), a 69.6% catchable throw rate, and two picks. Overall, Young (among 34 qualifying passers) is 13th in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, 26th in catchable throw rate, and 12th in hero throw rate. If Young is going to bounce back this week, he’ll have to do so against a solid Green Bay pass defense. Since Week 3, Green Bay has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per attempt, the fourth-lowest passing touchdown rate, and the seventh-lowest CPOE. Green Bay during that stretch also has had the 12th-lowest pressure rate, so Young should have clean pockets this week. It’s a good litmus test matchup to see if Young has turned back into a pumpkin prior to Halloween. It’s possible that Kincaid has a solid game this week, but the coverage structure isn’t in his favor. Baltimore has the fifth-highest rate of two-high (62.4%). Against two-high, Kincaid’s TPRR has fallen to 19%, and his YPRR sits at 1.23. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt. Wan’Dale Robinson (WR) Wan’Dale Robinson is the WR54 in fantasy points per game with three outings this season with at least 11 PPR points. Robinson has a 20.2% target share with 1.15 YPRR, eight red zone targets, four deep targets, and a 25.9% first-read share. His FD/RR is a solid 0.084. Cincy has been bleeding out production to slot receivers. Perine has mustered a decent 10.3% explosive run rate and 2.29 yards after contact per attempt this season. Tennessee has fielded a putrid run defense recently. Across their last five games, Tennessee has allowed the fourth-highest explosive run rate, the fifth-highest rushing success rate, and the seventh-highest yards before contact per attempt. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the tenth-highest explosive run rate, the third-most yards before contact per attempt, and the eighth-most yards after contact per attempt. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers. Since Week 5, Flournoy has had a 13.8% target share, 1.96 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 12.2% first-read share. Arizona has the highest two-high rate in the NFL (70.5%). Since Week 5, against two-high, Flournoy has seen his TPRR increase from 14% to 18% while posting 1.78 YPRR. Flournoy is a solid flex option this week. In their last five games, Arizona has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the sixth-most fantasy points per opportunity to slot receivers. Jake Ferguson (TE) Over the last two games, Jake Ferguson ‘s usage has been worrisome. Since Week 6, he has had a 54.1% snap rate, a 51.2% route share, a 4.9% target share, and only one first-read target. Yes, across their last five games, Arizona has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the seventh-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends, so Ferguson is on the fringe of streaming tight end options. I’m not starting him this week unless you truly are out of options, though.
